transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-29
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Harborline Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (Infra), Naoki Sato (Security)

Summary (auto):
High-level POC scoping focused on characterizing Harborline's workload for a pilot of Redwood Dedicated/Private. Discussed: QPS baselines, concurrency, input/output token distributions, tail latency targets, benchmarking approach, security constraints and timeline. Agreed next steps include sharing replay harness and sanitized traces.

Topics: workload shape, burst patterns, token skew, replay harness, success criteria, security/VPC/KMS, timelines

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Can we do quick intros and then jump into the workload you guys are seeing in production?
[00:00:12] Priya: Sure, Priya here. I run ML infra and model ops for Harborline. We use LLMs for several features — freight quoting, document understanding and real-time routing hints.
[00:00:22] Tom: Tom, infra. We're the platform team that owns the inference endpoints and autoscaling.
[00:00:27] Naoki: Naoki from security, I'll be asking about data residency, KMS, and audit logs.
[00:00:33] Marco: Marco, SE at Redwood. I'll focus on benchmarks and replaying your traffic.
[00:00:38] Lena: Great. Priya, can you paint a picture of the workload? QPS, average tokens, peak patterns?
[00:00:47] Priya: Yeah, high level — baseline QPS is about 25 requests per second across all features, but it spikes. For quoting it's more chat-like so input tokens average 160, output maybe 220. For docs parsing it's bigger — input can be 1.5k to 4k tokens, output 100–300 depending on extraction. Concurrency we see ranges from 30 to 120 concurrent connections depending on time of day and market events.
[00:01:12] Marco: Helpful. Do you have typical burst shapes? Are bursts short 10s-of-seconds or more sustained minutes?
[00:01:19] Priya: Both. Pricing events produce microbursts, 20–45s spikes. But after an outage or pricing engine job we get multi-minute elevated rates — 5–10 minutes.
[00:01:32] Tom: Also regional overnight batch jobs create sustained throughput around 2–3x baseline for about an hour.
[00:01:40] Lena: Ok so we need to characterize both microburst tail latency and sustained scaling behavior. What are your SLOs?
[00:01:47] Priya: For interactive features we want P95 < 250ms and P99 < 600ms ideally. For batch-ish routes we can accept higher latency up to 1.5s. Cost is a constraint though — we want predictable unit cost.
[00:02:00] Marco: Understood. For POC we usually run two types of benchmarks: replay (your anonymized traces) for realistic tail behavior and synthetic stress tests for mapped QPS/concurrency envelopes. Replay gives you realistic token distribution, which is critical for caching/KV hit patterns.
[00:02:16] Priya: Replay sounds good. We have recent request logs and token counts per request — we can sanitize and remove PII.
[00:02:22] Naoki: Quick callout on security: we can only share traces via a customer-managed S3 with KMS encryption. Also we need Redwood to support VPC peering for the Private option; alternative is Dedicated with strict egress rules.
[00:02:36] Lena: We support a private control plane and can accept S3 uploads encrypted with your KMS keys. We'll add the VPC diagram and the Private deployment security brief in the follow-up bundle.
[00:02:46] Tom: Good. Back to the workload: token skew — what percent of requests are small chat vs large doc parsing?
[00:02:54] Priya: Approximately 65% small chat/short prompts (<300 tokens total), 25% medium (300–800), 10% large (>800). But the large ones dominate token volume and cost. Also long responses have higher KV cache reuse but also increase average latency.
[00:03:11] Marco: That's a common profile. For sizing it's important to capture token-mix and concurrency envelope; the P99 tail often comes from overlap between large requests and microbursts. We'll run a replay and also a synthetic phase where we inject 80% short requests with 20% long, then invert the mix to observe tail behavior.
[00:03:29] Priya: Can you map that to hardware? We're evaluating Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted cost comparisons.
[00:03:35] Marco: Sure. For initial pilot we recommend a Dedicated pod with a mix of GPU types depending on your model. If you need guaranteed throughput at P99 targets during bursts, Dedicated with reserved capacity is safer. For Private we can do a VPC/on-prem package but that adds ops integration and slightly longer lead time.
[00:03:52] Lena: Cost note — quantization and batching policies will change token throughput. Marco, we'll propose a config set: quantized 4-bit profile for doc-heavy routes, batching windows tuned to sub-100ms for interactive routes.
[00:04:03] Marco: Right. Also prefix/KV caching will help the chat paths if prompts have common prefixes. For quoting, we saw a 15–25% token reduction with prefix caching in similar customers.
[00:04:13] Tom: How do you measure cache effectiveness in the replay?
[00:04:17] Marco: We'll instrument cache hit metrics in the runtime during replay. The harness will emit per-request token counts, KV hit/miss, latency quantiles and GPU utilization.
[00:04:25] Priya: What's the expected time to run the replay and produce sizing recommendations?
[00:04:30] Marco: Once we have sanitized traces, a 24–48 hour window for orchestrating replays across a few configurations, then a results analysis session — so roughly one week end-to-end to an initial recommendation.
[00:04:42] Lena: For the pilot success criteria, Priya, what are you measuring? Is it strictly latency and cost or also functional correctness?
[00:04:49] Priya: Three things: 1) Meet P95/P99 latency targets for interactive routes, 2) total inference cost per 1k tokens aligned with or better than our current provider, and 3) no regression in model output quality for extraction tasks. We'll provide a golden set of prompts for quality checks.
[00:05:05] Marco: We'll run an automated eval on the golden prompts pre and post-quantization and report metrics like exact match/F1 where applicable.
[00:05:12] Naoki: For compliance we need audit logs of requests, key rotation policies, and proof of SOC2. Also need table of ingress/egress IPs if we're going to whitelist.
[00:05:22] Lena: We'll include SOC2 report link, routing IPs for Dedicated, and an architecture diagram showing audit log paths. We can also support HSM-backed KMS for Private deployments but that's an add-on.
[00:05:33] Tom: One operational question — in sustained hour-long peaks, do you recommend autoscaling or pre-warming reserved capacity?
[00:05:41] Marco: A hybrid. Autoscaling handles organic load, but for predictable batches pre-warming reserved nodes reduces cold-start risk and provides capacity guarantees for tail SLAs. For the POC we can test both modes via the replay harness.
[00:05:53] Priya: How do you simulate microbursts with the harness? We want accurate tail behavior, not just smooth ramp-ups.
[00:05:59] Marco: The harness supports configurable burst profiles — Poisson, periodic spikes, and recorded timestamps so we can replay real inter-arrival times including milliseconds. That preserves concurrency overlap.
[00:06:12] Priya: Great. For the long docs, do you recommend model chunking or longer context models?
[00:06:18] Marco: Tradeoffs. Chunking reduces per-request tokens and may be cheaper if you only need parts of the doc, but it increases request count and concurrency. Longer context models reduce calls but increase per-token compute and memory. We'll evaluate both in the synthetic phase.
[00:06:33] Naoki: Any implications for KV cache if you chunk?
[00:06:36] Marco: Yes — chunking reduces KV reuse across chunks but can still benefit if chunks share context. We'll surface cache hit rates in the report.
[00:06:44] Lena: Let's talk success metrics again and timeline for the POC. We want a 4–6 week pilot: week 0 onboarding and trace handoff, week 1 replay and initial benchmarks, week 2 longer stress and config tuning, week 3 final run and business review. Does that align with your internal timeline?
[00:07:01] Priya: That's reasonable. We'd like to have a commercial decision by end of Q2 — so a 6–8 week runway is acceptable.
[00:07:09] Tom: Are there any infra constraints: egress restrictions or whitelisting?
[00:07:13] Naoki: We can allow egress to Redwood's Dedicated endpoints but Private will require VPC peering and specific IP ranges. I'll send a list of internal security must-haves.
[00:07:24] Marco: Noted. We'll also recommend a handshake for the KMS flow — either Redwood encrypts with customer public key or we set up cross-account KMS if you're on AWS.
[00:07:34] Priya: For the quality evaluation, we'll send a 500-sample golden set and the acceptance thresholds for extraction accuracy.
[00:07:40] Marco: Perfect. We'll include eval scripts so you can run locally and compare with the baseline.
[00:07:45] Lena: Anything else on risk or blockers?
[00:07:48] Naoki: Data residency for EU customers is a future ask. For this pilot US-only is fine, but call that out in docs. Also need indemnity language, but that's legal.
[00:07:59] Lena: We'll flag EU residency as a constraint and include legal contact.
[00:08:03] Priya: One more question — how do you handle model rollouts during the pilot? If we change model versions, do the benchmarks remain comparable?
[00:08:11] Marco: We version everything and pin model artifacts. For comparisons we freeze a commit hash of the model and runtime config. If you want to test a newer model, we run differential benchmarks and include regression alerts for latency and quality.
[00:08:23] Priya: Good.
[00:08:25] Lena: Ok let's summarize and confirm action items. We've already captured next steps in the notes but I'll recap: Redwood will send the replay harness and config examples, pricing matrix, security docs; Harborline will sanitize and upload traces and send golden prompts and compliance checklist. We'll schedule the first replay run the week of Apr 12 and a results review within 48 hours of finishing.
[00:08:48] Tom: Sounds good.
[00:08:50] Priya: Thanks everyone. I'll aim to get traces to you by Apr 5.
[00:08:55] Naoki: I'll send the security constraints doc by Apr 8.
[00:08:59] Marco: We'll prepare two initial configs: Dedicated baseline and a quantized Dedicated alternative; run both during replay.
[00:09:08] Lena: Great. Thanks all — we'll follow up with the bundle.

End of transcript.

Artifacts referenced:
- Replay harness (link to be provided)
- Security brief + VPC diagram (will attach in follow up)
